item.title: Healey Inherited a Better UK Budget Than He Thinks
item.description: John Healey’s job of presenting his first budget as chancellor of the Exchequer may not be enviable, but the one person he cannot blame is his predecessor. In terms of growth, fiscal consolidation and market sentiment, Rachel Reeves and former Prime Minister Keir Starmer left him a decent hand to play. The International Monetary Fund expects the British economy to expand by 1.3% this year, the second-fastest rate in the Group of Seven.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: Kemi Badenoch Is Having a Great Time as the Latest Heir to Thatcher
item.description: If the worst job in British politics is leader of his majesty’s loyal opposition, nobody told Kemi Badenoch. Since becoming Conservative leader in 2024, months after the party’s worst election defeat, Badenoch has often had to put up with being eclipsed by Nigel Farage and his hard-right Reform UK. Her success in battling that is impressive.
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince

item.title: Trump Should Reject Putin’s Plan for a Great Powers Summit
item.description: The mere prospect of Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump meeting for a great-powers summit while at the Asia Pacific Economic Community’s annual gathering next month is causing concern among America’s traditional allies, not to mention Ukraine. Rightly so.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Anthropic, Please Get on With Your IPO to Soothe the AI Trade
item.description: While the future is always uncertain, some market moments can feel sketchier than others. The wobble in the artificial intelligence trade reflects several near-term issues troubling investors, including elevated oil prices, rising interest rates, geopolitical anxiety and the imminent listing of AI behemoth Anthropic PBC. Some of these will get resolved sooner than others — but the latter will provide the acid test for sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Chris Hughes

item.title: Keynes, Yeats and Freud Enter the Group Chat
item.description: Around here, we respect the ancient texts.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: China Isn’t Killing Its Open AI (Yet)
item.description: China spent the better part of two years getting the world hooked on its cheap, open artificial intelligence models. Now, a surprise proposal for new export controls is stirring anxiety that Beijing may pull the plug on these tools that so many have come to depend on.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Thorbecke

item.description: Also derivative accounting, onions futures and Goldman hours.

item.title: AI Agents Are a Bigger Threat to Bank Deposits Than Stablecoins
item.description: Banks found it relatively easy to fend off the crypto bros. Artificial intelligence agents may prove a lot harder to tame.
item.dc:creator: Andy Mukherjee

item.title: SpaceX and Tesla — a Strange, But Certain, Merger
item.description: One rationale for merging SpaceX with Tesla is that the ever-busy Elon Musk could do just one earnings call per quarter instead of two. Hardly decisive, perhaps, but the conceit of prioritizing his preferences is salient enough. Talk of combining Space Exploration Technologies Corp. with Tesla Inc. overshadowed the quarterly calls of both companies this week. The results, however, illustrated just how odd this merger would be.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: Governments Must Not Test Limits of Global Economy's Resilience
item.description: Somewhat unexpectedly, the global economy has weathered the challenges of the past few years extraordinarily well. Following the pandemic, shock followed shock — Russia’s war on Ukraine, Washington’s rejection of rule-based liberal trade, then most recently the war with Iran. Any one of these might’ve led you to expect a severe economic setback, let alone all three combined. Yet global output kept on growing.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: In You Can See Everything, Nathan Fielder Feeds Our Grifter Obsession
item.description: When it comes to pop culture centered on Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced former CEO of the health technology startup Theranos, audiences clearly want all they can get.
item.dc:creator: Miles Surrey

item.title: Supreme Court Originalism Is Blinding Justices to Real-World Harm
item.description: If there’s ever been a strategic thinker on the US Supreme Court, it’s Justice Elena Kagan. So you can be absolutely certain that there was careful thinking behind Kagan’s pointed criticism of the court’s conservative majority in a public interview Tuesday at Catholic University’s law school in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Noah Feldman

item.title: Trump Deserves the Political Blowback for Inflation
item.description: Of all the factors dragging down Republicans’ odds of success in the coming midterms, inflation seems to be the most important. According to the Real Clear Politics aggregation of polling results, 70.1% of Americans disapprove of President Donald Trump’s handling of inflation, and just 27.3% approve. Inflation also consistently ranks as one of the top two or three issues on voters’ minds.
item.dc:creator: Justin Fox

item.title: The Good Guys Notch a Victory in the AI-Cybersecurity Era
item.description: The headlines were unremarkable. Researchers had found a way to weaponize two vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language used for websites and apps, and companies were being urged on Wednesday to install a patch. A smattering of websites and services were taken offline while it was installed. The US said it was looking into government systems and expediting mitigations. The media barely blinked.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: You Can See Everything Highlights the Challenge of AI Whistleblowers
item.description: There’s a scene in the new Elizabeth Holmes pseudo-documentary You Can See Everything that Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz says almost made him jump out of his chair and yell at the screen.
item.dc:creator: Beth Kowitt

item.title: It’s AI 0, German Philosophers 1
item.description: It might sound like a Monty Python sketch updated for 2026: Artificial Intelligence vs. German philosophers. The question to be settled is what it means to be human in an age when AI becomes more intelligent than we are.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kluth

item.title: Vivek Ramaswamy’s Cruel Campaign Ad Goes Too Far
item.description: For much of the Donald Trump era, no low has been too low for what passes as political rhetoric. Posting an AI slop video of the president dropping poop on protesters from a fighter jet? That’s “satire.” Calling Puerto Rico a “floating island of garbage”? Hilarious. Disparaging women as “incapable” and even “piggy”? That’s just telling it how it is.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith
